Hi Anita / Tom -

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap & next steps from our discovery:  

Summary of needs we heard:
- Primary requirement: Strong data isolation controls for customer data (audit logs, strict egress rules, SOC 2 evidence).
- Preference leaning toward a private deployment (VPC) due to regulatory controls, but want to understand cost/ops tradeoffs vs dedicated capacity.
- Network requirements: ability to bind everything to customer VPC subnets, no public egress, optional on-prem option for air-gapped workloads.
- Timeline: contract decision targeted by end of Q3.

Technical clarifications we promised to follow up on:
1) What data persists on Redwood-managed components vs customer-only storage (KV caches, logs, model telemetry).
2) How traffic flows when using Private VPC vs Dedicated (what hops are managed by Redwood).
3) What access controls & proofs (KMS integration, dedicated CPE, SOC 2 docs) are available for Private/on-prem.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-vpc-quicksheet.pdf (high-level diff), VPC-Architecture-Diagram.pdf (example topology).

Tom / Anita -

Great - confirmed for Tue 6/16 14:00 PT. Dev (copied) will lead the call on the network/data flow side.  

Short answers to your questions ahead of the call:  
- Private VPC: customer-managed networking + optional private control plane. No customer raw inputs are stored on Redwood-managed shared storage. Any persisted artifacts (model KV cache snapshots, logs) can be pushed into customer-owned S3 and encrypted with customer KMS. We'll bring the specific config options to the call (IAM roles, bucket policies, and KMS key IDs).
- Dedicated capacity: resources are reserved for your tenant, but the control plane is still hosted. We do have ephemeral caches on the inference nodes for performance; for customers with strict isolation needs, we offer configurations to periodically flush caches and to ship logs to customer-owned endpoints. If stricter guarantees are required (zero-data residency on Redwood nodes), Private (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended path.

During the call we'll cover: exact network flows (NAT, egress blocks), how KMS integration works for model telemetry and logs, and the set of SOC 2 artifacts we can provide.  

I've attached a short diagram in case helpful. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa
